title: The growing year
subtitle: From winter to harvest
objectives: Put the stages of the vine's year in order
Explain the risks at each stage

steps.title: The cycle
steps.body: In the northern hemisphere, the vine rests in winter. Buds break in March or April. Shoots and leaves grow, then the vine flowers in late May or June. Flowers that are pollinated become berries, called fruit set. In late summer the berries soften and change colour. Harvest comes from September to October.
steps.highlight: Budburst, flowering, fruit set, veraison, harvest

steps.title: Veraison and ripening
steps.body: Veraison is the moment berries soften and change colour: black grapes turn from green to purple, white grapes become translucent. From then on, sugar rises fast, acidity falls, tannins and aromas mature. This takes about 6 to 8 weeks, depending on the weather and the grape.

steps.prompt: Put the stages of the vine's year in order.
steps.explanation: Rest in winter, then buds, flowers, berries, colour change and finally harvest.

steps.title: Risks along the way
steps.body: Spring frost can kill young shoots after budburst. Cold, wet weather at flowering leads to poor fruit set, called coulure, or uneven berries, called millerandage. Hail can shred leaves and fruit. Rain near harvest can swell berries and cause rot. Each stage has its danger.

options: When berries soften and change colour
steps.explanation: Veraison is the start of ripening, marked by colour change and softening. Budburst and flowering come months earlier.

steps.title: What you learned
points: The vine moves from dormancy to budburst, flowering, fruit set, veraison and harvest
Veraison marks the start of ripening, when sugar rises and acidity falls
Frost, poor fruit set, hail and rot threaten each stage
